subject.title: fix(android): move device identity key into encrypted storage

question: Should this Android identity migration land only after every corrupt-legacy cleanup path verifies plaintext removal, plus a real device/emulator upgrade proof of identity continuity?
rationale: The intended security boundary is encrypted storage as the sole owner, while an existing upgrade workflow may retain private-key material if cleanup fails; accepting that tradeoff is a maintainer security decision.

options.title: Repair and prove before merge
options.body: Check deletion failure in the corrupt-legacy path, add regression coverage, and attach redacted Android upgrade evidence before landing.

options.title: Accept residual cleanup risk
options.body: Land with the known risk that an undeletable corrupt legacy file may retain plaintext material, documenting why that is acceptable.

options.title: Pause the migration
options.body: Hold the PR until the Android storage owner confirms the desired failure and recovery semantics.

recommendation.title: Repair and prove before merge
recommendation.body: Check deletion failure in the corrupt-legacy path, add regression coverage, and attach redacted Android upgrade evidence before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the proposed Android identity migration and is the closest available routing candidate from the supplied commit history.
